subject: Specter capacity footprint and surge trajectory — model mix & headroom ask
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Specter capacity ask: quick baseline numbers needed

Kimberly / Ben,

Following the discovery with Specter (Alyssa), they gave a mid-range projected util profile for year 1: 1.2M active monthly users, peaks concentrated in US-west, and an expected steady-state average of ~18M tokens/day with phasing to 60M tokens/day at peak events (model fan-out). Their SLO asks: p95 latency <= 350ms for single-turn completions and 99.9% availability under committed throughput.

They plan to run two prompt classes: short assistant-style completions (~40 tokens/client average) and longer summarization jobs (700 tokens average) — traffic mix about 75/25. They want us to propose dedicated capacity (reserved) with a burst buffer for product launches.

Request: can you run a quick model mix footprint and tokens/sec -> GPU mapping with the following constraints:
- Primary model: quantized 13B variant for most traffic (low-latency)
- Fallback/large-model: 70B 8-bit for summary class when higher fidelity required (quantized, KV cache friendly)
- Target p95 <= 350ms for 13B, 95% of requests should meet 200ms for single-turn small completions
- Add explicit burst runway for 3x baseline peak for up to 30 minutes

I've attached an initial spreadsheet (specter_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) with the customer numbers. Ben — can you populate tokens/sec per-GPU, p95 tail estimates, and a recommended slab count + headroom percentage? Kimberly — please flag any thermal/placement constraints if we need heterogeneous GPU pools (A100p vs H100) for 70B workload.

I did a quick back-of-envelope: 13B quant @ 2.5k tokens/sec per A100p (continuous) when using batching and prefix KV caching for 75% short completions; 70B quant at ~600 tokens/sec on H100 with quant kernels. That's very rough — want engineering verification.

Thanks,
Jonas

On Sat, May 30, 2026 at 09:12, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Kimberly / Ben,
> 
> Following the discovery with Specter (Alyssa), they gave a mid-range projected util profile for year 1: 1.2M active monthly users...

Thanks for the context — ran a short sizing pass against our benchmark kernels and the attached sheet. High level summary (assumptions below):

Assumptions
- Short completion = 40 tokens output, avg 80 input tokens -> total 120 tokens per request
- Long summary = 700 tokens output, avg 350 input -> total 1050 tokens per request
- Traffic mix: 75% short, 25% long by request count (as you said)
- Baseline steady-state tokens/day = 18M -> tokens/sec baseline = 208.3 tokens/sec average over 24h; peak day events -> 60M tokens/day -> 694.4 tokens/sec average on peak day
- Peak burst requirement (customer asks for 3x baseline peak for 30m) -> short-term tokens/sec target = 2083 tokens/sec

Per-GPU throughput (measured on internal perf harness with current quant kernels and batching):
- A100p (13B quant optimized, continuous batching + KV cache): 2,900 tokens/sec sustained for short completions; 1,200 tokens/sec mixed (when mixed with mid-size sequences). p95 latency at 2,900 t/s for short requests ~ 170-210ms.
- H100 (70B 8-bit quant kernels, larger KV): ~700 tokens/sec sustained for long-completion heavy batches; p95 latency at 700 t/s for long requests ~ 300-380ms (depends on sequence length).

Recommended model split + fleet mapping
- Dedicated pool A (13B quant on A100p): handle 90% of short completion volume and opportunistic long requests when cheap. Nominal target capacity: sustain 2,500 tokens/sec aggregate (headroom included). Using 2,900 tokens/sec/GPU -> need 1 GPU for small pilot, but for committed dedicated we'd carve a slab of 8 GPUs (gives ~23,200 t/s nominal) — that is overkill for year1 but gives runway. Practical committed slab: 4 x A100p (gives ~11,600 t/s nominal) to cover steady-state + peak headroom for short completions with grouping and batching.
- Dedicated pool B (70B on H100): reserve 2 x H100 for scheduled heavy summary windows; at 700 t/s each, 2 GPUs -> 1,400 t/s (enables handling of the 25% long mix during peaks if we offload some long runs asynchronously).

Sizing math (rounded)
- Baseline peak tokens/sec target (peak day): 694 t/s -> majority short: 520 t/s short, 174 t/s long.
- Steady headroom target (x1.5) -> short cushion = 780 t/s, long cushion = 260 t/s.
- Recommended slab: 4 x A100p (handles short traffic with 1.5-2x buffer) + 2 x H100 (handles long summaries with room).

Burst runway (3x baseline peak for 30m)
- Burst requirement ~2083 t/s. We should propose: Dedicated base slab (4A100p + 2H100) + burst pool on shared capacity (hosted or reserved burst) to absorb ~1.3k t/s for 30m. Practically: enable burst to 8 additional A100p-equivalents during launch windows.

Latency fit notes
- With 4x A100p we comfortably hit p95 <= 350ms for short completions; 95% within 200ms is achievable with proper batching and KV cache warm-up.
- For long summaries p95 ~350-450ms on H100 at high concurrency; suggest softer SLO or asynchronous batch slot for >700-token jobs, or use a quantized distilled 30B variant if they need synchronous 350ms tight SLO.

Operational asks
- Can we carve the 4xA100p as a dedicated slab (monthly) and propose 2xH100 as reserved with scheduled warmup windows?
- Need Kimberly to confirm thermal placement/availability for mixed-sku sizing and whether we can guarantee colocated routing for cross-GPU fallbacks.

I added a new sheet in the attached spreadsheet with per-GPU t/s numbers and the slab proposals. Happy to refine.

—Ben

ben@redwood.ai

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@specter.ai>

Jonas / Ben,

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifications from our side before we take to procurement: 

1) We prefer synchronous responses for both short and long requests for the first 6 months; if that pushes latency over 350ms on long jobs we'll consider a staged rollout.
2) For budget reasons the initial committed slab will likely be modest; procurement will push for 4x A100p and 0x H100 initially, with the option to add H100s for scheduled summaries. Can you show a phased plan that starts with 4x A100p dedicated + hosted burst (8 equiv) for launches, and an optional add-on of 2x H100 at month 3?
3) Can you provide an operational runbook for KV cache warmup, canary steps for launch, and a fallback policy to route >700 token jobs to asynchronous queue if H100s aren't provisioned?

If you can turn the above into an explicit phased commitment (month 0: 4xA100p + burst; month 3: add 2xH100) with estimated monthly costs and expected p95 latencies per phase, procurement will be able to sign faster. Also please include any SLA exceptions for burst funding and a short note about DBR/thermal constraints for colocated pools.

We should target a sign-off call next week.

Best,
Alyssa Chen

- Ben: produce a phased proposal (PDF) that lists month-0, month-3, month-6 configurations with per-phase token/sec budget, expected p95 latency, and cost estimates. Include an optional 30-minute burst sizing line and the fallback policy text. (Target: EOD 2026-06-01)
- Kimberly: confirm whether we can guarantee colocated routing for 4x A100p and add notes about thermal constraints and lead time for ordering H100s if Specter opts to add them in month 3. Also include recommended availability zones (us-west-2 preferred) and any cross-region considerations.
- I'll draft the SLA addendum and a short canary checklist (KV cache warmup windows, perf gating, 10% traffic canary for first 48 hours). I'll circulate the signed draft and the procurement-friendly cost table.

Alyssa — we'll get the phased PDF + runbook and send a calendar invite for sign-off next week.
